english: From Peter’s letter: “There were also false prophets… who will bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them.” (2 Peter 2:1) For we were bought at a price “not with perishable things, silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ.” (1 Peter 1:18–19) So we belong to the one who purchased us, even while we serve the living and true God. How, then, is Christ not God — the one we have enrolled as Master, and know as living and true?

“And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true one, and we are in the true one, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.” (1 John 5:20) Jesus Christ is not understood as the Word from God the Father naked, by himself, and outside flesh; but when he became human, then he was also named Christ Jesus. So when he himself is the true God and the eternal life, who among those who think otherwise will put up with it?

From Jude: “While I was making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write appealing to you to contend for the faith once for all delivered to the saints (Jude 1:3). For certain people have crept in… who pervert the grace of our God into sensuality and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.” How does someone who once believed deny our Lord Jesus Christ? english: …of God. For if as many as received the Son “he gave authority to become children of God,” (John 1:12) as the evangelist says, those who have not received him would not be counted among God’s children, not having known the one through whom this exists.

“And who is the one who conquers the world if not the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ — not in the water only, but in the water and the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth. For there are three who testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three are the one.” (1 John 5:5–10) The one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God conquers the world; and who Jesus is, the disciple himself makes clear to us saying: “This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ.” But he also speaks of blood and of Spirit, and says the three are the one. So the Word became flesh, and he sanctifies us by the Spirit, and cleanses by the blood, and washes again with clean water; and the Son is altogether one, whose we also say the Spirit and the water and the blood are.

“If we receive the testimony of humans, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, that he has testified about his Son (1 John 5:9). The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself; the one who does not believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that he has testified about his Son.” And the Father has testified to the Son through the Spirit and through a voice.
